summary: Feed s140_double is degraded for NDR: 8.7% TCP packet loss (genuine drops, not slicing) and 12.4% frames sliced to ~256 bytes. Both break full-payload flow reassembly required by this NDR, reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Genuine packet loss in the visibility path - 170 of 1959 TCP packets (8.7%, threshold 1%) show gaps via TCP sequence analysis. Slicing was ruled out by IP-length validation, so this is not an artifact. Most likely SPAN/mirror oversubscription or packet broker buffer drops under burst, before the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot reassemble flows or perform stream reassembly and signature matching; missing segments cause incomplete sessions, missed detections and false negatives for lateral movement/exfiltration. High severity for NDR that needs both directions and full payload.

recommended_fix.why: TAP delivers line-rate, lossless copy without SPAN buffer drops or oversubscription. Eliminates the 8.7% gaps at the source; if TAP already in use, add aggregation and load_balance/filter to prevent broker drops.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing enabled - 261 of 2105 frames (12.4%, threshold 5%) cut short, most to 256 bytes. Broker is truncating payload to save bandwidth/tool load, but this NDR profile requires full payload.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR loses L7 payload beyond 256 bytes; cannot do deep packet inspection, file extraction, or exploit detection. Truncated flows appear as incomplete and evade NDR analytics.

params.target: disable slicing for NDR feed s140_double

recommended_fix.why: NDR needs_full_payload=true. Disabling slicing restores full packets for detection. If bandwidth to 10G tool port is constrained, use selective filter or dedicated NDR feed instead of global slicing.
